notes.cutoff: Data cut-off: this edition covers Thursday evening to Sunday morning, before Sunday's EGX session opens, so the latest close is Thursday 12 November (EGX30 52,023.37). Brent, WTI and gold are Friday's settlements. Gold prices in EGP are Banky's Sunday prices. Bullish and bearish tags are directional reads of the news, not trade recommendations.
notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: e-finance's nine-month results, because Arab Finance's article body refers to 2025 while its page is dated 2026; Thursday's investor flows (Amwal Al Ghad gives them in billions of pounds) and breadth, so those charts are dropped; a second source for Thursday's index closes; the cost of the Ras Shokeir wind farm, not disclosed; Brent against the budget's oil assumption; the reserves split between foreign currency and gold. Banky's gold page shows 12 November in its header but 15 November in its body.

items: Trump says the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vance to drop the talks, while the blockade stays → the end of diplomacy keeps Gulf energy at risk; oil ends the week at $96.13 and European gas jumps 12%.
European gas surges 12% in a week to €96.18/MWh, and Goldman sees €150 in early 2027 if Gulf LNG stays disrupted → costlier LNG raises Egypt's energy import bill and costs for gas-heavy industry.
Gold has its worst week since March, down 4.7%, and 21K gold in Egypt falls 2.7% to EGP 5,950 a gram → markets see a December Fed hike as certain, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 ends the week at 52,023, up about 1.7% (derived), led by banks → QNB Egypt rises four sessions in a row and Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% on Thursday.

Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 on Thursday after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran's attack on a US radar in Bahrain → renewed attacks on Gulf energy put oil back near $96, a cost for Egypt's import bill.
Gold falls to a 13-month low and is down 3.5% this week; 21K gold in Egypt drops to about EGP 5,975 a gram → markets fully price a December Fed hike, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023 on Thursday, while Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% → blue chips take profits after a strong week; banks with earnings news still rise.
Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn as interest income grows about 43% → high rates keep lifting bank income.

Israel's security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, and Tehran threatens bases from West Asia to Europe → a renewed war would hit oil, Gulf shipping and the pound just as markets price a wind-down.
Eastern Company's nine-month profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn, and the stock gains 4.17% → sales rise 11% and margins widen, which supports the stock.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 on Wednesday after two days of gains, with turnover at EGP 11.79 bn → the rally pauses as small caps take profits; fertiliser stocks rebound.
The government targets public debt of about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and frees a Red Sea plot to help pay it down → lower debt would ease debt-service costs over time.
EGX30 jumps 2.08% to 52,483 on Tuesday, a second day of gains, with EFG Holding up 6.75% → slower inflation and foreign buying of Egyptian T-bills lift sentiment.
Remittances rise 20.4% to a record $13 bn in July to September, and reach $38.2 bn in the first nine months of 2026 → the largest source of dollars for Egypt keeps growing despite the regional war.
Hotter US inflation and a hawkish Waller make a December Fed hike nearly certain → a higher US rate narrows the carry on Egyptian debt and lifts the cost of Egypt's floating-rate loans.
Foreign investors buy about $614.7 mn of Egyptian T-bills on Monday while selling stocks → the carry trade returns, which supports the pound.

Urban inflation slows to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, a nine-month low, while core inflation eases to 13.1% → the CBE's 20% deposit rate is now about 7.3 points above inflation (derived), giving it room to hold on 17 December.
Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday after Trump calls the Iran war effectively over → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,415 on Monday, but foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn → local investors drive the gains while foreign money takes profits.
Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn → profit grows far faster than sales, which supports the stock's valuation.

stories.h: Egypt's final IMF review moves online with $2.3 bn at stake and a 15 December deadline
stories.what: The IMF mission to Cairo, from 25 October to 5 November, ends without a staff-level agreement, and talks on the final review of the $8 bn Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility move to virtual meetings. Completing both reviews would unlock about $2.3 bn, and the programme expires on 15 December. "Important progress was made during the mission," says IMF communications director Julie Kozack, who leaves any follow-up programme to the Egyptian authorities.
stories.why: The sources do not say which issues remain open.
stories.aff: IMF funding, the pound, Egypt's credit outlook and foreign appetite for local debt.
stories.eg: A deal before 15 December would close the programme cleanly; a delay would raise uncertainty over the pound.
stories.egx: Neutral now; a missed deadline would be bearish for banks and foreign-held blue chips.

stories.h: Telecom Egypt's profit jumps 43.7% and Elsewedy's rises 20.7% in nine months
stories.what: Telecom Egypt's consolidated net profit rises 43.7% to EGP 24.38 bn in January to September, and operating revenue rises to EGP 93.57 bn from EGP 78.32 bn. Elsewedy Electric's consolidated net profit rises 20.7% to EGP 15.30 bn on revenue up 31.7% to EGP 263.03 bn. Telecom Egypt closes Thursday at EGP 133.00 and Elsewedy at EGP 120.70.
stories.why: Revenue growth drives both results; Arab Finance gives no further breakdown.
stories.aff: Two large listed companies in the brief's table.
stories.eg: Strong results from large listed companies support the index into the new week.
stories.egx: Bullish for Telecom Egypt and Elsewedy Electric.

stories.h: ENGIE-led group with Orascom closes $588 mn of debt for a 900 MW wind farm
stories.what: ENGIE (35%), Toyota Tsusho's Aeolus (40%) and Orascom Construction (25%) reach financial close on the 900 MW Ras Shokeir wind farm with about $588 mn of non-recourse debt; JBIC lends up to $285 mn. The first 300 MW is due in January 2028 and the rest by the third quarter of 2028. The group's wind capacity in Egypt rises to 1.8 GW from 912.5 MW.
stories.why: The project signed a 25-year power purchase agreement in March 2026 and has been under construction since June.
stories.aff: Power supply, gas use and Orascom's order book.
stories.eg: About 4 TWh a year of wind power reduces the gas Egypt burns for electricity.

stories.h: Iran targets a US base in Bahrain again as oil ends the week near $96
stories.what: Iran says it targets a US base in Bahrain and Bahrain issues threat alerts, while the Saudi-led coalition says it shoots down three Houthi drones. Brent settles at $96.13 on Friday and WTI at $88.92, up for a third day but down about 2% on the week.
stories.why: With US-Iran talks stalled, Iran and the Houthis keep up attacks on Gulf targets.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: Oil near $96 keeps Egypt's fuel import bill high.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers and energy users.

key.l: 21K gold per gram in Egypt, Sun 15 Nov

stories.h: Gold in Egypt edges up after its worst week since March
stories.what: Banky puts 21K gold at EGP 5,975 a gram on Sunday, up 0.25%, and the gold pound at EGP 47,800. Spot gold settles at $3,884.77 on Friday, down 4.7% on the week, as traders give a December Fed hike about 90% odds for a quarter point and 10% for a half point.
stories.why: Hot US data push up Fed hike expectations and the dollar.
stories.aff: Local gold prices and household savings.
stories.eg: Lower gold prices make the metal cheaper for Egyptian savers.
